_: What the control room looks like (dev-docs/poltergeist/control-room.md, 3.5).
This file is data. tools/gen-control-room-look.py turns it into
tools/the-control-room-look-is-one-set.py is red when either is out of step.
Lengths are points, times are seconds. These are readings off the design, not off a product.
Every value names where it was read (`src`, a key of `sources`); a group's `_src` covers the
values in it that name none. A value the user has not ruled on carries `tentative`, with the
other candidate, so that ruling on it is one edit here and both hosts follow.
A colour is `#RRGGBB`, or `#RRGGBB@a` with a from 0 to 1.

sources.v15-panes: design v15, src/style.css and src/06-panes-l.html, checked against 06-panes.png
sources.v18-a: design v18, direction A: src/v18.css and CHANGES.md
sources.v19-q3: design v19, way three: src/v19.css and CHANGES.md
sources.supervisor: the supervisor's ruling, not a design file
sources.undesigned: not in the design: chosen while building the mac list, to be ruled on
sources.v17-contrast: design v17, src/contrast.md (measured off the rendered pictures)

font._doc: Type sizes. Nothing is set smaller than `min`.

body.doc: Body text, tab titles, the terminal.

group_name.doc: A group's name in the list.

weight_emphasis.doc: The selected tab, a status word, a title.

line._doc: The only two widths there are.

stroke.doc: The plus and the cross; the rail of the time band.

window.doc: The system's; drawn as 14 in the design.

row.doc: 12 = 6 + 6: concentric with the panel through its padding.

supervisor_inner.doc: The terminal inside the supervisor's frame: 12 - 4.

worker.doc: 8 until v15: everything 8 from the window's edge is 12.

window_edge.doc: From the window's edge to anything.

supervisor_bezel.doc: The supervisor's border, and its gap to the terminal inside.

terminal_text_inset.doc: Left and right of the terminal's text.

window_tab._doc: A window tab holds three things: close, title, one status glyph.

side_slot.doc: The width kept on each side, so the title stays centred.

working_glyph_shown.doc: Whether a working terminal's spinner is drawn on a window tab. Off, so that every glyph in the row of tabs is one to look at.

tentative.why: The design drew it; the supervisor chose not to. The user has not ruled.

width.doc: Wide enough that what a row waits on is 322 across: 41 characters of the terminal's face, which is one step of most commands. The user, 2026-10-13: "A is better, it can be wider".

quiet_row_height.doc: A group that needs nothing: one line.

separator_space_above.doc: Below the last waiting row's own gap.

row_line1_height.doc: The glyph, the name, who is waiting and the status word. A waiting row is this, then its lines of what it waits on, inside `row_padding_y` above and below: 60, 80 or 100 high for one, two or three lines.

ask_line_height.doc: One line of what a row waits on.

fix_line_height.doc: The line under a card that reads Failed, holding its Fix button (task 1560) and, when the last press was refused, why: a regular-size push button at the menu's font, which does not fit in `ask_line_height`.

tentative.why: Not in the design. 28 is the room the retention notice's OK takes; 24 would fit a small button, whose font is under the menu's.

ask_max_lines.doc: How many lines what a row waits on may wrap to. A sentence takes up to this many and ends in an ellipsis. A command of this many steps or fewer gives every step a line first, and what is left over to the steps that need a second.

tentative.why: The design's direction B drew four. The user chose A, which draws three.

ask_max_steps.doc: A command of more steps than `ask_max_lines` is not cut to that many lines: every step keeps one line, cut at its end, so the start of every step shows. Past this many the last line says how many steps are not shown, rather than dropping them without a word.

tentative.why: 3 is the design's cap applied to steps as well, which hides the fourth step of a command behind an ellipsis -- the step that may be the dangerous one. The supervisor ruled that out; where the ceiling is, nobody has.

ask_cells_per_line.doc: How many characters of the terminal's face one line of what a row waits on holds: the count a host uses when it has no font to measure with. A wide character is two.

status_word_gap.doc: Between a glyph and its word.

pane._doc: The three frames a split can wear.

name_role_gap.doc: Between a pane's name and the word for what it is. Measured 9 to 10 between the ink; the boxes are 8 apart.

plain_title_inset_x.doc: An ordinary terminal's title, from its pane's left edge. Measured: ink at 13.

plain_title_band_height.doc: The title is centred in a band this high at the top of the pane, with nothing drawn behind it. Measured: ink from 9 to 22 below the pane's top.

supervisor_floats.doc: It has a shadow; the other two do not.

stack_tab._doc: The tabs over a cell that holds several terminals.

inset.doc: From the content's left and right edges to a tab's body: corner 8 + straight 4 + arc 8. Also the terminal text's inset.

tentative.why: At 16 the arc's foot meets the end of the corner and the two read as one S.

reverse_arc_radius.doc: The arcs that join the current tab's foot to the content.

overlap_below.doc: How far the current tab's fill runs past its foot, to cover the strip's line.

trailing.doc: From the status at the right end of the strip to the strip's right edge. In a supervisor's frame this is measured inside the border, like `inset`.

status_gap.doc: The least between the plus and the status at the right end.

more_button.doc: The `more` button that stands for the tabs there was no room for, between the last tab and the plus: the dots, and beside them the place for the glyph of the most pressing terminal among those it stands for (6 + dots 14 + 4 + glyph 14 + 6). The place is kept whether or not there is a glyph, so that the strip does not move when one of them starts waiting.

tentative.why: The design draws no strip with more tabs than fit. 28 is the dots alone, as wide as the plus, with nothing to say that somebody behind them is waiting.

more_glyph_gap.doc: Between the dots and the glyph beside them.

nominal_cell_width.doc: How wide one character of a tab's name is taken to be where there is no font to measure with: what the two hosts are held to one answer by. A wide character is two.

min_width.doc: The narrowest a tab is squeezed to before the rest go behind a `more` menu at the right end. 104 is the design's eight-letter tab: at that a name keeps seven characters and its ellipsis.

tentative.why: 68 is the design's three-letter tab (padding 12 + three cells + gap 8 + glyph 14 + padding 12): more tabs stay on the strip, and each is one letter and an ellipsis. The design draws no squeezed strip; where squeezing stops has not been ruled on.

quota._doc: The allowance block at the bottom of the list: a hairline, then one opened-out part for each account at or past the limit line, then the one line. 38.5 high on an ordinary day, 88.5 with one account close, 112.5 with one used up and a way out named.

separator_space_below.doc: Under the hairline that closes the list above.

line_height.doc: The one line: the label at the left, each account and its number at the right.

entry_gap.doc: Between two accounts in the one line.

label_gap.doc: The least between the label and the accounts.

alert_title_height.doc: Which account and which window and how much, and at the right when it comes back.

alert_glyph_gap.doc: Between the triangle and the words, when it is all gone.

bar_min_fill.doc: The least of the bar that is filled, so that a filled end is always a round one.

note_line_height.doc: The way out, under the bar of an account that is used up.

status._doc: The four status glyphs and how they move. Nothing moves under Reduce Motion.

waiting_pulse_period.doc: Only the one that has waited longest pulses.

problem_shake_distance.doc: Left and right, once, on entering the state.

working_spin_steps.doc: It steps; it does not turn smoothly.

working_spoke_width.doc: One of the spinner's short lines, on the artboard.

working_spoke_inset.doc: From the artboard's edge to a line's outer end.

working_spoke_min_opacity.doc: The faintest line; the brightest is 1 and the rest step up to it.

done_unseen_dot.doc: The dot's diameter on the artboard: a size smaller than the other glyphs.

elsewhere._doc: A terminal that is being shown somewhere else: the last frame it drew here, frosted, under the sentence that says where it went. The whole of it is one button.

blur.doc: How far the kept frame is blurred, as the sigma of a Gaussian in that frame's own pixels: enough that no word of it can be read.

veil.doc: How much of the terminal's ground is laid over the whole blurred frame. At 0.65 the frame can still be told for the screen it was (the supervisor, on build-18: at 0.86 it was "a flat colour and a line of words" again). The words are not kept readable by this; `shade` does that.

tentative.why: The user has seen neither on a real terminal; 0.86 is where the veil alone keeps the words at 4.5:1 and the frame is a faint shadow.

shade.doc: How much more of the terminal's ground there is behind the two lines of words, at the corners of their box -- where there is least of it under them. With the veil, 0.867 of the ground is under the words there: both lines keep 4.5:1 over any frame at all, white or black, in both themes. It is more than this at the middle and less everywhere further out: it has no flat part and no edge.

shade_spread.doc: How fast the shade falls away from its middle: the sigma of a Gaussian, as a fraction of the shade's radius. At the radius it is gone.

shade_words_within.doc: The shade's radius each way is at least the words' half-width (half-height) divided by this, and at least half the place's shorter side: so the corners of the words' box are never further out than 0.37 of the radius, where 0.65 of the middle's amount is left (the supervisor, on build-19: it read as a plate with an edge; it should read as the middle being a little deeper).

frame_longest_side.doc: The frame is kept no larger than this on its longer side, in pixels: it is only ever shown blurred.

selection._doc: The selected row of the group list and the selected window tab: a chip at rest, glass while it slides.

edge_band.doc: The width of the faint band just inside the chip's edge.

spring_damping.doc: Below 1, so it overshoots (about 4%) and settles.

tentative.why: Whether the chip overshoots at all has not been ruled on; 1 is critically damped.

lift_in.doc: How long the chip takes to lift when it starts to move.

lift_scale_window_tab.doc: The window tab's chip is the system's own piece of glass; this is how much of it the slide adds while it is in the air.

lift_lands_with_remaining.doc: The chip starts back down when this much of the way is still to go.

settled_within.doc: The slide is over once it stays this close to its end, as a fraction of the way: 0.41 s with the period and damping above; the design says about 0.45.

slide_samples_per_second.doc: The window tab's slide is handed to the system written out as this many positions a second.

glass_at_rest.doc: Whether the row's chip is the system's glass while it sits still. Off: at rest it is a plain bright piece with nothing live behind it, and the glass is only there for the slide.

tentative.why: Glass that sits still is recomposited whenever what is behind it changes; the one measurement of glass over a scrolling terminal found a cost in full screen. The user has not ruled.

stretch_along.doc: At most, with speed, along the direction of travel.

centre_zoom.doc: The middle of the chip while lifted.

refraction_shown.doc: Whether the chip's edge bends what is under it while it slides. It is the system's glass that bends it, where the system has one (macOS 26); nothing here moves pixels itself.

tentative.why: The other candidate keeps the lift and the slide and drops the refraction. What the system's glass looks like over the rows has not been seen in a window.

seen_after.doc: How long a row stays selected, with the control room in front, before its group counts as seen.

tentative.why: 0 marks it seen the moment it is selected, so arrowing past a row would clear it.

refraction_strength_rest.doc: A fraction of the band's width; strongest at the edge, falling off as the square.

selection_tint.doc: How much white the chip mixes in, at rest.

selection_edge.doc: The band inside the edge: darker when negative, lighter when positive.

selection_shadow_blur.doc: As the design's animation takes it; its still pictures use about twice this as a CSS blur.

selection_halo_blur.doc: A second shadow with no offset.

window_base.doc: The window's ground. The design lays two faint blooms over it.

attention.doc: Blue, something for you: the glyph of waiting and of done-and-unseen.

attention_text.doc: The same blue as a word or a number.

problem.doc: Red, something is wrong: the glyph.

problem_text.doc: The same red as a word or a number. See `text_on` for where the word is not red.

side_panel_highlight.doc: A hairline along the top edge.

supervisor_edge_focused.doc: Light: the outer edge darkens. Dark: a ring is added just inside it.

surface_row.doc: Measured: an unselected row as it comes out over the panel. For contrast, not for painting.

surface_window_tab.doc: Measured: an unselected window tab on its track.

symbol._doc: The system symbols the glyphs are. Working is the system's progress spinner, which has no symbol name. `held` is the supervisor's ruling (the design says only `a pause glyph`).

_doc: Which colour a status word is written in, by the surface it sits on.
Dark red text does not reach 4.5 on the lighter dark surfaces, and lightening the red makes it
another colour. So there the word is written in the main text colour and the red is left to the
glyph and the minutes. That is the whole of this table, and the hosts read it rather than decide.

tentative.why: The other candidate accepts a contrast of about 3. The user has not ruled.

_doc: What is drawn on what, for the contrast report (`gen-control-room-look.py --contrast`).
`text` needs 4.5, `large` (20 pt bold) and `glyph` need 3. `problem_word` is the status word
